_doc: PER-SHOT FRAMING RULINGS for townmap/dellhollow.cameras.json — a TEMPORARY sidecar.
Everything in here belongs in cameras.json itself: `pins.<id>` merges onto that
camera's record and `defaults` merges onto its defaults. It lives in a separate file
only because the agent that introduced exit-seam framing (legibility follow-up,
2026-07-30) was not permitted to edit cameras.json. THE COORDINATOR SHOULD MOVE IT:
add "pin": true to the boatyard camera, add "frameExits": false to defaults (and
delete it when the re-bake lands), then delete this file — tools/cine_solve.mjs reads
`cam.pin` / `defaults.frameExits` either way, so nothing else changes.
pin: true — this frame is a HUMAN RULING. The solver reproduces its authored pos/aim
exactly and excludes it from the exit-seam constraint, so a pinned shot re-solves to
itself byte for byte. Requires pos+aim on the camera (a pin with nothing to pin to is
defaults.frameExits: false — the whole town opts OUT of framing its exit seams. A
MIGRATION flag only: turning it on re-aims most shots, and a town whose backdrops are
already baked cannot absorb that until its re-bake pass. `--frame-exits` overrides it
for a proposal run; new towns get exit framing by default and should never need this.

defaults._why: del-cine's 17 backdrops are baked against the current solved frames; exit framing re-aims 12 of them, and the re-bake is a separate, single pass (docs/qa/review/solve-proposal/).

boatyard._why: The user-accepted v10 hero frame. Its exit seam to waterfront sits at ndc y -1.15 and stays there: re-aiming this shot is the user's taste ruling alone, not a solver's.
